units.title: Gears, Torque and Wheels
units.blurb: How motors turn into force and speed.

units.title: Frames and Kinematics
units.blurb: Where things are, from the robot's point of view and the world's, and where an arm's hand ends up.

topics.title: Gear Ratios
topics.short: A small gear driving a big one trades speed for torque by the ratio of their teeth.
topics.trouble: Students divide the wrong way and make the slow gear faster.

topics.title: Torque and Choosing a Motor
topics.short: Torque is force times lever arm; a motor must beat the load's torque, m g L, with room to spare.
topics.trouble: Students forget that holding a load farther out takes more torque, or mix up grams and kilograms.

topics.title: Wheels and Speed
topics.short: Rolling speed is angular speed times radius: v = ωr, and rpm must be turned into radians per second first.
topics.trouble: Students multiply rpm by the radius without converting to radians per second.

topics.title: Coordinate Frames
topics.short: A point seen by the robot becomes a point on the map by a rotation and a shift.
topics.trouble: Students add the robot's position but forget to rotate by its heading, or rotate the wrong way.

topics.title: Forward Kinematics of a Two-Link Arm
topics.short: Given the joint angles, the hand is at x = L1 cos θ1 + L2 cos(θ1 + θ2), y = L1 sin θ1 + L2 sin(θ1 + θ2).
topics.trouble: Students use θ2 alone for the second link instead of θ1 + θ2.

topics.title: Inverse Kinematics of a Two-Link Arm
topics.short: Given where the hand should go, the law of cosines gives the elbow angle; there are usually two answers, and sometimes none.
topics.trouble: Students forget to check that the target is in reach, or miss the second, elbow-up solution.
